items.prompt: State what a dry run is.
items.canonical_answer: A dry run traces the code by hand on paper: the tester executes it statement by statement without running it, recording each variable’s new value after each statement in a trace table.

items.prompt: Explain why a trace table exposes a logic error that a program’s running does not.
items.canonical_answer: A logic error runs happily and delivers the wrong result, so running the program shows a healthy program - the fault is invisible from the outside. The trace table records what the program actually does, variable by variable and statement by statement, so the traced values can be compared with the values the problem required, and the first row where they differ is the statement that causes the error - which is what running alone never shows.
marking_guidance: Reason: a logic error runs and looks healthy, so running hides it - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the traced values are compared with the required values, because the first differing row names the causing statement - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 12.3 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A till program totals six sales but the printed total is one sale short. Explain how a dry run locates the error.

marking_guidance: Context: this given till program with its short total - 1 mark for the dry run tracing the loop.
Reason: because the trace records the loop finishing after five sales, the first differing row locates the error at the loop’s bound, so the trace table names the statement - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Explain why alpha testing precedes beta testing.
items.canonical_answer: Alpha testing is in-house: the development team’s own users run the whole system, so the faults they find are fixed before any outsider meets the program. items.prompt: Explain one benefit of including extreme data in a test plan.
items.canonical_answer: Extreme data is valid data at the limits of the acceptable range, so it tests the edges the program must still survive: twelve nights where twelve is the maximum, an age of 100 where 100 is the top of the range. A program that works for the middle of the range can still fail at the last valid value, so the extreme tests show the range is exactly right at its edge - which is a benefit the ordinary data of the middle never delivers.
marking_guidance: Benefit: the valid limits are tested, so the edges of the range are shown working - 1 mark.
Because a program can work in the middle and fail at the last valid value, the extreme test catches the edge fault, so the edge belongs in the plan - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Explain one limitation of a test plan whose data is all normal.
items.canonical_answer: Normal data is valid data in the ordinary range, so the whole plan tests only the middle of the specification: the rejection of invalid data goes untested, because abnormal data is missing, and the edges of the range go untested, because extreme and boundary data are missing. A program can pass such a plan and still accept what it should reject and mishandle the last valid value - the plan certifies the easy half and is silent about the rest.
marking_guidance: Drawback: only the middle of the range is tested, so rejecting and edge-handling are untested - 1 mark.
Because abnormal and boundary data are missing, a passing program can still fail the invalid and the last valid value, so the plan proves less than it seems to - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Describe the difference between corrective and perfective maintenance.
items.canonical_answer: Corrective maintenance fixes errors found in use - a fault, something broken, repaired; whereas perfective maintenance improves a working program that meets its requirements - an improvement, nothing broken, made better. One responds to a fault and the other to a wish, so the difference is the program’s state: broken against working-but-improvable.

The summary screen is perfective maintenance: the program meets its requirements and the users want it better, so the work improves a working program. The need does not end, because the world keeps moving - laws change, systems are replaced, users keep seeing improvements they want - so a program is not finished being maintained, which is why the maintenance stage continues for the program’s whole working life.

items.prompt: A vet’s dose program is tested. Write pseudocode for a function DoseCheck that takes the real Weight in kilograms and returns TRUE when the computed dose is safe, FALSE otherwise - the dose is Weight times 12 milligrams, and a dose above 300 milligrams is not safe; a weight of 0 or less is also not safe, because no animal was weighed. The function is the test’s oracle: black-box tests will call it with data chosen from the specification alone.
items.canonical_answer:
```pseudocode
FUNCTION DoseCheck(Weight : REAL) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Dose : REAL
   IF Weight <= 0 THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF
   Dose <- Weight * 12
   IF Dose > 300 THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ELSE
      RETURN TRUE
   ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
```
marking_guidance: Mark point 1: the function heading with the parameter and its type, RETURNS BOOLEAN, and ENDFUNCTION. Mark point 2: the declaration of Dose.

Mark point 3: the selection guarding the invalid weight, Weight <= 0, returning FALSE, because a weight of zero or less is abnormal data the program should reject. Mark point 4: the dose computed from the specification’s rule, Weight times 12.
Mark point 5: the safety selection with the condition Dose > 300, a complete comparison. Mark point 6: FALSE RETURNed above the limit and TRUE below it, both branches returning.

Mark point 7: the limits consistent with the black-box data the specification allows - 25 kilograms gives exactly 300, returning TRUE, because 300 is the limit, not above it. Mark point 8: the function complete and closed - one parameter in, the Boolean verdict back through RETURN, never output.

context.situation: A vet’s dose check as the black-box test’s oracle.

(c) After a year of use, the ministry’s account format grows a digit, and the dispensary also asks for a weekly stock screen. Name the maintenance form of each work. [2]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) A logic error: the program runs, breaks no rule of the language and stops at no operation, so it looks healthy - the wrong total only shows in the result, because a logic error is found by comparing the printed value with the required one, never by the program failing.
(b) Boundary row: quantities 4, 5 and 6 either side of the top limit, expected accept, accept, reject - because the bound set wrongly fails exactly at the edge. Abnormal row: quantity 0 (or -1), expected reject - because invalid data the program should refuse is required behaviour.
(c) The account format is a change in the environment around a working program, so the work is adaptive maintenance. The weekly stock screen improves a working program that meets its requirements, so the work is perfective maintenance.
marking_guidance: Part (a): the reason for the type - 2 marks, 1 per point: logic named, because it runs and only the result is wrong.
Part (b): the context of the given range - 2 marks, 1 per point: the boundary trio with its expectations, the abnormal value with its rejection.
Part (c): the state of the program in each situation - 2 marks, 1 per point: adaptive for the changed environment, perfective for the improvement.
